under Section 10(A) of the Divorce Act, 1869, which is applicable

to the parties and reads as under:­

 "10A Dissolution of marriage by mutual consent.

 thereunder, a petition for dissolution of marriage may be

3 It is heartening to note that the parties have amicably





resolved the dispute before the learned Mediator and the final

terms and conditions of the settlement mutually arrived at

between the parties are as under:­

1. That by way of a decree of divorce/annulment of
 marriage between the parties, their marital status will be
 severed. For the said purpose the parties will take



 appropriate legal steps either by converting the petition
 for divorce filed before the learned court below into a joint




 petition (if otherwise permissible) or by filing appropriate
 petition/application before an appropriate court and, if





 permissible, before the Hon'ble High Court of Himachal
 Pradesh in the present FAO No. 2 of 2019. Soul and only





 intent of the parties is that their marital status will come
 to an end for all intends and purposes.

2. That the parties admit, acknowledge and declare that
 they are well settled in life and are capable of supporting
 themselves independently. However, for Master Raphael
 Daniel, son of the parties, who presently is in custody of
 respondent Ms. Mary David, Sh. Sandeep Daniel
 (appellant herein) will pay a lumpsum amount of Rs.

10,00,000/­, which will satisfy all the legal obligations on
 the part of Sh. Sandeep Danial (appellant) towards the
 maintenance, upbringing, education etc of the aforesaid




 .

minor son and also all legal obligations, past or future





 whatsoever, on any count towards his minor son Master
 Raphael. Once this amount is deposited in the Bank





 Account No. SBA 373201501574 IFSC No. ICIC0003732,
 ICIC Bank Jalandhar, of Master Raphael, the same will
 be converted into a Fixed Deposit Receipt in the name of





 minor son under the guardianship of the mother Ms.
 Marry David and such Fixed Deposit Receipt will not be
 encashed till the minor son attains the age of majority

 except with the permission of the Court. However, the

 periodical interest on the Fixed Deposit Receipt will be
 paid to the mother for the maintenance and upbringing of
 the child. In addition to the aforesaid 10,00,000/­ to be



 paid to the minor son, the appellant shall pay another
 sum of Rs. 10,00,000/­ to his wife, respondent Smt. Mary




 David by depositing the same into her Bank Account No.
 65038968792, IFIC No. SBIN0050657, State Bank of





 India, Bathinda Cantt Branch. This payment to the
 respondent will be in discharge of all legal obligatins and





 liabilities of the appellant towards present, past and
 future claims whatsoever of any kind on any count
 including future maintenance/alimony once for all of Ms.
 Mary David.

3. On payment of aforesaid amount of Rs. 20,00,000/­, the
 consequential decree for divorce will be passed between
 the parties. The amount of Rs. 10,00,000/­ into the Bank
 Account of the minor son will be deposited immediately




 ::: Downloaded on - 29/09/2019 00:24:51 :::HCHP
 4


 within a period of 15 days from the date when the
 Hon'ble Court accepts this settlement between the
 parties. Also an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/­ within the




 .

same period will be deposited into the account of the





 respondent. The balance amount of Rs. 5,00,000/­ due to
 the respondent will be paid and deposited into her





 account by the appellant within a further period of one
 month thereafter.

4. That the pending petition before the Hon'ble Punjab and





 Haryana High Court which has been filed by the
 appellant Sh. Sandeep Daniel herein will be withdrawn
 and the order of maintenance impugned therein in the

 said petition will also be got set aside by mutual consent

 of the parties, in view of the fact that the appellant has
 already paid towards the maintenance of the minor son
 entire amount due. The maintenance amount already



 paid to the minor child will not be claimed back by the
 appellant Sh. Sandeep Daniel. However, in view of the




 present settlement and also the fact that the very orders
 of maintenance passed by Family Court, Bhatinda, on the





 basis of present settlement no consequential benefit shall
 be claimed by the minor son or the mother, respondent, in





 future. The appellant will not be under any legal
 obligation to further pay any amount either under the
 aforesaid maintenance order of the Trial Magistrate to
 minor son or to the respondent.

5. That the pending CRMM No. 29158 of 2018 titled
 Sandeep Danial Vs. Raphael Danial and Another before
 the Hon'ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana, on the
 strength of the present settlement will be withdrawn by




 ::: Downloaded on - 29/09/2019 00:24:51 :::HCHP
 5


 the appellant Sh. Sandeep Daniel and also Ms. Mary
 David, respondent herein, undertakes and agrees to
 withdraw CRM No. 233­19 before Principal Judge Family




 .
Court Bhatinda.

6. That the parties will jointly file an application for disposal
 of the aforesaid case by mutual consent for setting aside





 the order of maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C
 passed in favour of Master Raphael.

7. That in view of the fact that permanent arrangement by





 way of the present settlement for the maintenance and
 upbringing of the minor son of the parties has been made
 by paying Rs. 10,00,000/­ to the minor son, the

 respondent has also assured and undertaken that she

 being an earning hand, if need be, shall also settle and
 maintain aforesaid minor son in case such exigency
 arises despite the present settlement. Likewise all other



 connected ancillary proceedings pending anywhere
 especially in any court in Bhatinda for the recovery of




 maintenance amount will also be withdrawn in view of
 the present settlement.

8. That the parties have agreed that Sh. Sandeep Daniel
 will have visitation rights to visit and see minor son of the





 parties namely Master Raphael at Bhatinda or at any
 other place where the said minor child will be residing in
 future alongwith his mother. Such visitation rights shall
 be exercised once a month at the discretion of the
 appellant Sh. Sandeep Danial and that too preferably on
 a school holiday of the minor child between 12 PM in the
 afternoon to 4 PM in the evening with prior intimation to
 the respondent. If at any time the parents of the




 ::: Downloaded on - 29/09/2019 00:24:51 :::HCHP
 6


 appellant(grand parents of Master Raphael) accompany
 the appellant during the exercise of the visitation right,
 the respondent will have no objection for the same and




 .
the grand parents will also be entitled to meet the child.

Depending on the outcome of the exercise of such
 visitation rights, the appellant will be free to get the





 schedule of visitation refixed or redetermined or
 rescheduled by the Hon'ble High Court of Himcahal
 Pradesh through appropriate application in the present





 FAO No. 2 of 2019.

9. That the respondent Ms. Mary David has also undertaken
 to withdraw the proceedings filed against the appellant

 Sh. Sandeep Daniel under Section 125 Cr.P.C from the

 court of Principal Judge Family Court, Bhatinda without
 any further consequence or adjudication of any kind.

10. The parties and the parties have agreed to abide by



 aforesaid terms and conditions and in accordance with
 the same a settlment deed will be filed before me on the




 next date. Any of the parties backing out from the
 aforesaid settlment will be liable for contempt of court in





 addition to the other legal consequences which may
 follow in favour of the respective parties from the present





 settlment.

11. That the learned counsel for the parties have further
 undertaken to file the joint settlment deed before me on
 the next date of hearing in accordance with the aforesaid
 settled terms. A copy of today's proceedings be also
 supplied to learned counsel for the parties so as to enable
 them to file settlement deed in aforesaid terms. Since the
 respondent travels to Shimla from Bhatinda and also the




 ::: Downloaded on - 29/09/2019 00:24:51 :::HCHP
 7


 fact that Unit Examination of Master Raphael are to start
 in near future, as such, on the request of the respondent,
 which is agreeable to the appellant, the proceedings will




 .

be held next on 24.6.2019. The parties will remain





 present with the required documents and settlment deed
 on the said date positively.

12. Signed, executed and filed this 13 th Day of May, 2019
 by the learned counsels under instructions of their clients.

4 It would be noticed that the parties have one minor

child, Master Raphael Daniel and it has specifically been recorded

in the settlement that the same is in the best interest of the

minor.

5 I see no reason to disagree with such settlement as an



amount of Rs.10,00,000/­ has already been deposited in ICICI

Bank by way of fixed deposit in the name of Master Raphael




Daniel and further amount of Rs.5,00,000/­ has also been paid to





the respondent, receipt whereof has been acknowledged by the





respondent in the open court. Now, only balance of

Rs.5,00,000/­ remains to be paid, for which the petitioner No.1,

Sandeep Daniel, has undertaken to pay the same to petitioner

no.2, Mary David, on or before 5.8.2019.

6 It is not in dispute that the parties are living

separately since 2012 and in fact divorce petition was filed on




 ::: Downloaded on - 29/09/2019 00:24:51 :::HCHP
 8


5.8.2016. Once, it is duly established on record that they have not

been able to live together and now that they have parted their




 .

ways by arriving at one time settlement, then I am of the





considered view that there is no impediment in dissolving the





marriage of the parties by mutual consent.

7 Accordingly, the petition is allowed and the marriage

between the parties is dissolved under Section 10(A) of the Indian





Divorce Act leaving the parties to bear their own costs. Decree

sheet be prepared accordingly. Pending application(s), if any, also


stands disposed of.

8 Needless to say that since the petition is disposed of

on the basis of terms and conditions of the settlement mutually



arrived at between the parties, which have already been




reproduced hereinabove, therefore, it is made clear that in case





there is any non adherence to the terms and conditions of the

settlement any of the aggrieved party shall be at liberty to





approach this Court for the said purpose.

9 Before parting, this court expresses its gratitude to the

valuable assistance rendered by the learned Mediator, Mr. N.K.

Sood, Senior Advocate, in bringing about the amicable settlement

between the parties.
